# Judith Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:1** The next morning Holofernes gave the order: the whole army and every allied force was to march on Bethulia, take control of the mountain passes, and crush the Israelites.

**7:2** Every soldier broke camp that day. Their combined might came to one hundred and seventy thousand foot soldiers and twelve thousand cavalry — and that was not counting the baggage train and all the support personnel. It was an enormous army beyond measure.

**7:3** They poured into the valley near Bethulia, setting up camp beside the spring. Their lines stretched from Dothaim in the west to Belmaim, and from Bethulia all the way to Cyamon, which looks out toward Esdraelon.

**7:4** When the Israelites looked down and saw the sheer scale of the enemy force, their hearts sank. "These men will strip the land bare," they said to each other. "The high mountains, the valleys, the hills — none of it can contain an army this size."

**7:5** Every man armed himself. They lit warning fires on their watchtowers and stood guard through the whole night.

**7:6** On the second day, Holofernes rode out with his full cavalry force to reconnoiter the defenses of Bethulia.

**7:7** He surveyed the approaches to the city, found the water sources, seized them, and stationed armed guards over every one. Then he rode back to his command.

**7:8** The chiefs of the Edomites, the Moabite tribal leaders, and the coastal commanders came to him with a proposal:

**7:9** "My lord, hear us out — we do not want to see your army take losses here.

**7:10** These Israelites do not fight with spears. Their weapon is their terrain — those mountain heights are nearly impossible to scale.

**7:11** So do not attack them head-on. Not one of your men needs to die.

**7:12** Just sit tight. Hold your whole force in position. And send your men to take control of the spring at the foot of the mountain —

**7:13** that is the only water source for Bethulia. Cut it off and thirst will do your fighting for you. They will hand over the city. Meanwhile, we will climb the ridges nearby and camp there to make sure no one sneaks out.

**7:14** They will waste away — men, women, children, all of them — dying in the streets before a sword even touches them.

**7:15** And they will pay for their defiance, for refusing to come out and make peace with you."

**7:16** Holofernes liked what he heard, and so did his whole staff. He gave the order to implement the plan.

**7:17** The Ammonite force moved out, backed by five thousand Assyrian soldiers. They took the valley and cut off the water supply and springs.

**7:18** The Edomites and Ammonites climbed the highlands and set up camp facing Dothan. Part of the force fanned out toward the southeast, toward Egrebel, near Chous by the Mochmur stream. The rest of the Assyrian army spread across the plain like a flood, covering the whole face of the land — tents, equipment, soldiers, an almost incomprehensible number.

**7:19** The Israelites cried out to the Lord their God. Their spirits collapsed. They were completely encircled, with no way out.

**7:20** The Assyrian siege held for thirty-four days. Every water jar in Bethulia ran dry.

**7:21** The cisterns were going empty. They had less water than they needed for a single day, and what remained was being doled out by ration.

**7:22** The children went limp. Women and young men crumpled from thirst and collapsed in the streets and at the city gates. There was nothing left in them.

**7:23** The whole population — young men, women, children — converged on Uzziah and the city leaders and screamed at them before the assembled elders:

**7:24** "God will judge you for this! You have ruined us by refusing to make peace with the Assyrians.

**7:25** There is no one coming to help us. God has handed us over to them. We are going to die lying in the streets, dying of thirst, dying in shambles.

**7:26** Open the gates. Give the whole city over to Holofernes. Let them take what they want.

**7:27** Being plunder is better than being dead. Slavery means we live. At least we will not have to watch our babies die in front of us, or our wives and children gasping their last.

**7:28** We call heaven and earth and our God — the Lord of our ancestors, who is punishing us for our sins and the sins of our fathers — to witness against you. Do not let things come to this today."

**7:29** The whole assembly broke down weeping, crying out to the Lord God in a great wailing voice.

**7:30** Uzziah said to them: "Brothers — hold. Hold five more days. The Lord our God may still relent and show us mercy. He has not completely abandoned us.

**7:31** But if those five days pass and nothing changes — I will do what you are asking."

**7:32** He sent the crowd home. The men went back to the walls and towers. The women and children returned to their houses. And misery settled over every corner of the city.
